items.title: Alibaba's latest Qwen models routed some requests through company servers, researchers find
items.summary: Alibaba's Qwen 3.8 models tried to send data to the company's own cloud servers during testing. Palisade Research finds the behavior in three models from the 3.8 generation, while older models aren't affected. The likely cause: Alibaba's training infrastructure got baked into the models as a learned behavior. The article Alibaba's latest Qwen models routed some requests through company servers, researchers find appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Google Deepmind's Genie 4 puts a modern spin on agent designs that predate LLMs
items.summary: Google Deepmind has introduced Genie 4, a real-time world model that simulates interactive 3D worlds with sound and talking characters. Gemini models help plan in the background to keep the simulation consistent. Genie 4 is still an early research model, and longer sessions lead to visual inconsistencies. The article Google Deepmind's Genie 4 puts a modern spin on agent designs that predate LLMs appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Former Deepmind researcher thinks AlphaGo's playbook can cure AI hallucinations
items.summary: Former Deepmind researcher Thore Graepel wants his startup Metis Reasoning to bring AlphaGo's search principle to general reasoning. Instead of locking knowledge inside model weights, an explicit knowledge ledger would make every conclusion checkable against evidence. So far, though, there's no working system and no benchmarks. The article Former Deepmind researcher thinks AlphaGo's playbook can cure AI hallucinations appeared first on The Decode

items.title: OpenAI asks outside experts, including a Nobel laureate, to check proofs its AI produced in math, computer science, and physics
items.summary: OpenAI says its internal AI models have cracked three major open questions in math, computer science, and physics. One of them is part of a famous Millennium Prize Problem, each of which carries a $1 million prize. Outside experts, including a Nobel laureate, are now checking whether the proofs hold up. items.title: Anthropic uses its IPO letter to renew its pledge that Claude will never show ads
items.summary: Anthropic says it will keep ads out of Claude. In a cover letter accompanying its IPO filing, the company argues that the chatbot's sole incentive should be to provide helpful answers. items.title: OpenAI's Ted Sanders shares a rule of thumb for picking the right GPT-model
items.summary: OpenAI's Ted Sanders explains where GPT-6.1 Terra fits in the company's GPT lineup. The smaller model outperforms the larger Astra in technical communication and costs far less but trails it in most other areas. Sanders says model size, reasoning effort, and multi-agent systems are distinct dimensions that can’t be reduced to a single "IQ score." items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra halves OpenAI's API prices and still gains ground on its larger models
items.summary: OpenAI has released GPT-6.1 Terra, a mid-range model that cuts API prices in half compared to its predecessor. Analysts say it sets a new standard for intelligence per dollar, especially for everyday computing tasks and AI-driven computer control. items.title: Anthropic opens its books for Wall Street, showing record revenue and mounting obligations
items.summary: Anthropic is the first major AI lab to file an S-1 with the SEC, planning to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT." The numbers are strong, with $11.6 billion in quarterly revenue, a first-ever operating profit, and existing customers spending nine times more year over year.
